conventions.convention: The GNS inner product is ⟨A,B⟩σ = Tr(σ B* A), linear in its first variable, with σ strictly positive and Tr σ = 1. Detailed balance requires [Hs,σ] = 0 and self-adjointness of the dissipator D; the Hamiltonian commutator is kept separate and is anti-self-adjoint.
The gap theorem assumes ker D = C I. Its centered space is {A : Tr(σ A) = 0}; γ is defined only for d > 1. For d = 1 the centered space is zero and relaxation is trivial.

For d ≥ 2, wab is the rate from a to b, Lab = √wab |b⟩⟨a|, and (Wf)a = Σb≠a wab(fb−fa) acts on column observables. Row population vectors obey p′ = pW. Gibbs balance is πa wab = πb wba; the positive-rate undirected graph must be connected.

The recorded label path belongs to a separately selected energy-resolved instrument. Its holding rate in state a is ra and destination probabilities are wab/ra. Full AC is retained for the supplied joint-path construction; the one-time GKSL semigroup alone does not select this record law.

The response perturbation is Hε(t) = Hs − ε h(t)B, with ε dimensionless, h continuous and measured in joules, and B Hermitian and dimensionless. The dissipator is held fixed and the initial state is σ.
Record transport uses the stationary initial law π and real velocity labels with π(v) = 0. YT = ∫₀ᵀ v(a(s)) ds, and Drec uses Var(YT)/(2T), with units square metres per second.

Physical applicability of the adopted bath and instrument is restricted to the finite interval [0,tres]. All-time relaxation and infinite-time coefficients concern mathematical continuations. Rates and temperatures are adopted inputs, with no measured calibration or experimental evidence asserted.
Classical relative entropy uses the natural logarithm and the extension 0 log(0/πa) = 0. Its displayed derivative formula applies for t > 0, when all populations are strictly positive.

load_bearing.statement: For finite GNS detailed-balance data with faithful σ and ker D = C I, if d > 1 then D restricted to M0 = {A : Tr(σ A) = 0} has strictly negative eigenvalues and positive gap γ. For centered A and t ≥ 0, ‖e^(tG)A‖σ ≤ e^(−γt)‖A‖σ. Every density satisfies ‖ρt−σ‖1 ≤ ‖σ^(−1/2)(ρ−σ)‖2 e^(−γt). Centered correlations are absolutely integrable and their real diagonal resolvent coefficient is nonnegative. The d = 1 case is trivial without defining γ.

For d ≥ 2, finite energies, β > 0, nonnegative Gibbs-balanced rates, and a connected positive-rate graph, the jumps Lab = √wab |b⟩⟨a| give a dissipator self-adjoint in the σ-GNS inner product, [Hs,σ] = 0, and ker D = C I. The diagonal generator W is self-adjoint on L²(E,π), has constants as its kernel, and has a positive gap on π-centered functions. The generic detailed-balance gap theorem applies.
For finite GKSL data and a faithful density σ, define G(A) = i[Hs,A]/ℏ + D(A) and ⟨A,B⟩σ = Tr(σ B* A). The specified convention requires [Hs,σ] = 0 and ⟨D(A),B⟩σ = ⟨A,D(B)⟩σ for all matrices A,B.

For the connected Gibbs-jump data, the specified energy-resolved instrument uses no-click evolution e^(tK), K = −iHs/ℏ − R/2, and labelled jump operations √dt Lab. Its intended recorded path is the nonexplosive finite chain with holding rates ra, destination probabilities wab/ra, and transition matrix e^(tW), under full AC.

Assume full AC, connected finite Gibbs-jump data, the specified record initialized with π, and real centered velocity labels v. Then Eπ[YT] = 0 and Varπ(YT) = 2∫₀ᵀ(T−s)Cv(s) ds for every T ≥ 0. Moreover Cv has an exponential gap bound and limT→∞ Varπ(YT)/(2T) = ∫₀∞ Cv(s) ds = ⟨(−W|π⊥)^(−1)v,v⟩π ≥ 0.

Under the finite detailed-balance gap hypotheses with d > 1, a continuous Hamiltonian perturbation Hε(t) = Hs − ε h(t)B with fixed dissipator and initial state σ has response derivative ∫₀ᵗ h(s)RAB(t−s) ds, where RAB(τ) = (i/ℏ)Tr(σ[e^(τG)A0,B]). The kernel has the stated exponential bound and is absolutely integrable.

Adopts a specified finite time-independent GKSL state law physically on [0,tres], and separately adopts the selected energy-resolved instrument for the connected Gibbs-jump specialization. The same generator and instrument may be continued mathematically for all nonnegative times without asserting physical applicability beyond tres.

concerns.concern: Definition, outcome 2, asserts the normalized post-click state L_ab|a⟩/‖L_ab|a⟩‖ = |b⟩ without restricting to w_ab > 0; proof step 1.2 repeats the unconditional normalized-state assertion. The supplier allows zero rates. For example, take d = 3, all energies zero, w12 = w21 = w23 = w32 = 1 and w13 = w31 = 0. These rates satisfy Gibbs balance and connectivity, but L13|1⟩ = 0, so the displayed normalization is 0/0. The definition must restrict normalization to positive-rate outcomes or explicitly exclude zero-probability branches. The [cited quantum-jump source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/quant-ph/9702007), §IV.C, equations 127–128, conditions normalization on an emission being selected.
